title: Premium Body Care and Home Fragrance Competitive Landscape

scope.description: Premium and prestige businesses that compete for body care, bath, home fragrance, gifting, wellbeing, refill, and omnichannel beauty retail demand.
inclusionLogic: brands with direct participation in body care, bath, home fragrance, skincare-adjacent wellbeing, or luxury fragrance-led retail
global and regional players that materially shape category expectations for gifting, discovery, replenishment, refillability, and store service
specialist beauty retailers that act as discovery platforms and can substitute for brand-owned ecommerce or boutique journeys
caveats: Reported metrics are not directly comparable. Some companies report brand-level revenue, some report group-level beauty revenue, and some report parent-company or retail-segment metrics.
Where only parent-company or segment-wide data is public, the metric scope is preserved exactly and labeled accordingly.
Private brands often disclose fewer financial metrics; in those cases, only official public operating scale indicators are included.
Official store-locator counts are operational snapshots that can change quickly and should be treated as source-page observations rather than audited footprint metrics.

The Body Shop public careers-page operating scale appears to be legacy wording after ownership and restructuring changes, so it is included as official published context rather than a current audited footprint.
scope.selectedDomainRationale: Rituals, L'Occitane, and Molton Brown all operate in premium body care, bath, home fragrance, gifting, and wellbeing retail. The domain is therefore modeled as an omnichannel premium personal-care and home-fragrance business rather than as pure cosmetics, pure fragrance, or mass beauty retail.
